name: Turkey Alfredo Rotini Bake
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 6 servings, 513 cal, 38g protein, clears both gates as published. Five-ingredient white-sauce bake; the catalog's creamy turkey pastas are all tomato or cream-cheese based, none use jarred alfredo. Fully board-mapped and about as cheap as a pasta bake gets. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Five ingredients, one pan, and a cheese crust on top. Rotini, ground turkey, mushrooms, a jar of alfredo, and mozzarella, baked until the edges go brown and crispy, which everyone knows is the best part of any pasta bake. It is the cheapest bowl in this whole Italian run at about $1.83, and it still delivers 574 calories and 43 grams of protein a serving.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.14. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $25.61 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.83 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $31.60 across 14 servings, roughly $2.26 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.58 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $37.18. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.83 a container for a creamy baked pasta with 43 grams of protein in it. That combination is rare enough to be worth writing down.
shop_smart: Jarred alfredo is one of the great budget shortcuts. Homemade would need butter, cream, and a wedge of real parmesan, which costs more than triple and takes a whisk and your attention.
Mushrooms are the biggest produce line here. Buy whole ones and slice them yourself, since presliced costs more per ounce and dries out faster in the package.
Rotini is one of the cheapest boxes in the aisle. Buy three, because a pasta bake needs volume and dry pasta stores forever in a cabinet.
Mozzarella goes on top where you can see it, so this is the one place a full 16 ounce buy earns its keep. Watch for the buy two get one deals and stack your freezer.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the rotini about 2 minutes short of the box time and drain it. It will finish cooking in the sauce in the oven, and pasta cooked twice to full is mush.

Slice the mushrooms and cook them in a dry hot pan until they give up their water and it evaporates, about 8 minutes. Dry pan first, then season. That is how you get browned mushrooms instead of gray ones.
Add the ground turkey to the pan and brown it, breaking it up, with salt and black pepper, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Stir in the alfredo sauce and a splash of water, and let it warm through until it loosens into a pourable sauce.
Fold the drained pasta into the sauce so every piece is coated, then spread it into your baking pans.
Cover with the mozzarella and bake at 375F for 25 minutes, until it bubbles around the edges and the cheese has browned in patches.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then transfer it into your weighed pot for portioning.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is your per-container gram target. Scoop from different spots in the pan so the browned edge pieces get spread around, because those are worth fighting over. Each serving lands at 574 calories and 43 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from dizzybusyandhungry.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A creamy pasta bake for about $1.83 a container. This is one of hundreds. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Turkey alfredo rotini bake meal prep: five ingredient baked pasta with ground turkey, mushrooms, alfredo, and mozzarella. 574 calories, 43g protein, about $1.83.
head.keywords: turkey alfredo bake, rotini bake, baked pasta, turkey meal prep, budget meal prep, five ingredient dinner
steps: Boil the rotini 2 minutes short of done and drain.
Cook the sliced mushrooms in a dry hot pan until browned.
Add the ground turkey and brown it to 165F with salt and pepper.
Stir in the alfredo sauce with a splash of water.
Fold in the pasta, spread into pans, top with mozzarella, and bake at 375F for 25 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes and portion by weight into 14 containers.
